newsitem.title: UK: Archbishop of Canterbury speaks of retiring.
newsitem.headline: Archbishop of Canterbury speaks of retiring.

text.p: Archbishop of Canterbury George Carey, leader of the world's 70 million Anglicans, says he expects to retire in about five years time from what he calls a spiritually and physically demanding job.
Speaking in a British television documentary previewed on Thursday, Carey said there were times when he felt very tired.
"I feel fine now, but there is no doubt about it that in five years time I would be ready to hand over to someone else," said Carey, 61, who became Archbishop of Canterbury in 1991.

"I think it's a very wearing job. You pour yourself into it and it's not only the physical side of it, because there is a physical demand, but it is also spiritually and emotionally demanding because you are being hit from many different angles."
The documentary, to be shown on British television on Sunday, accompanies Carey on a visit to South Africa which marked the retirement of Bishop Desmond Tutu.
Tutu said Carey's appointment surprised many in the Anglican church. "He came in as someone many regarded as an upstart..." he said.
"But very quickly and disarmingly he has been able to establish his authority and part of it, I think, is that he's not stiff.
Tutu added: "The other bishops admire him, admire his leadership. He is relaxed and gives other people space to be themselves."
